2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that, the petitioner and his brother Mosadder Ali, who are wage-earners, purchased 4.00 acres of land appertaining to SS Plot No. 16, 316, 367, 368 and 370 of Khatian No. 20/2 from one Nirmala Chowdhury and Sundip Chowdhury by a registered kabala dated 30-7-1970 and since such purchase they are holding and possessing the said land. It has been also stated that since the petitioner and his brother were residing in the United Kingdom they could not mutate their names in the revenue records earlier and subsequently they mutated their names in respect of the aforesaid purchased land in Mutation Case No. 1518 of 1990 in the Office of the Assistant Commissioner. Land, Jagannathpur and got the mutated Khatian No. 34 in their names. It has been also stated that one Alkas Mia, who is inimical to the petitioner, made an application to the respondent No. 2 for cancellation of the Mutation. Case No. 1518 of 1990 on certain false allegation and though the respondent No. 2 did not have the jurisdiction to entertain such application, who became functus officio after allowing Mutation case and relief against the said order is available before the Assistant Commissioner by way of review or by an appeal to the Appellate Authority, entertained the said application of Alkas Mia and started Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1993-94 and passed an order on 18-9-1993 for issuance of notice upon the parties. The petitioner further asserted that although no notice was served upon him, the process server filed an incorrect report showing service return and on 25-9-1993 one Mastafar Ali filed an application praying for adjournment on behalf of the petitioner though the petitioner had no knowledge of any such application and adjournment was allowed by the respondent No. 2. Subsequently two dates were shown to have elapsed for filing objection by the petitioner though the petitioner had no such knowledge. The petitioner stated that he having learnt that the respondent No.2 had joined hands with his enemy filed an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sunamgonj and obtained an order of stay and the records of Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1993-94 of the Office of the respondent No. 2 was called for by order dated 16-10-1993 but in spite of the said order the respondent No. 2 most illegally recorded an order on 18-10-1993 in Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1993-94 modifying his previous order of mutation in favour of the petitioner and maintaining mutation of 0.8266 acres of land in the name of the petitioner and 4.13 acres of land out of 4.96 acres of land was ordered to be recorded in Khatian No. 1 treating the same as khas land of the Government. Photostat copy of the order sheet of the said Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1993-94 along with the petition has been annexed to this writ petition and marked Annexures 'C' and 'CI' respectively. 

 3. The petitioner, amongst other facts, also alleged that after he filed a criminal case, the said Alkas Mia in collusion with the respondent No. 2 got Miscellaneous (Eviction) Case No. 67 of 1993-94 initiated for eviction of the petitioner from the land of SS Plot No. 370 on the ground that the petitioner had been illegally making construction of a pucca latrine on encroaching the khas land of the government appertaining to Dag No. 370 of Mouza Dostpur. The petitioner further asserted thathaving initiated the said proceeding the respondent No. 2 issued a notice dated 15-12-1993 in Misc (Eviction) Case No. 67/93-94 asking the petitioner to stop further construction of the latrine and to show cause why he should not be evicted from the said land by 1-1-1994 in default whereof legal action would be taken against him, which is the impugned order contained in Annexure D to the writ petition. The petitioner appeared before the respondent No. 2 on 1-1-1994 and made a prayer for holding an enquiry by examining the papers of the petitioner stating that he is the owner by purchase of the property and Title Suit No. 14 of1993 was pending in respect of the schedule properties appertaining to Plot No. 370 (JL No. 165 of Mouza Dostpur). The petitioner has challenged the initiation of the proceeding being Miscellaneous (Eviction) Case No. 67 of 1993-94 by the respondent No. 2 and issuance of the notice as contained in Annexure 'D' and obtained the present Rule. 

 8. It appears from Annexure 'D' that the respondent No. 2 initiated the proceeding for eviction of the petitioner from plot No. 370 of khas khatian No. 1 on the prayer made by one Alkas Mia alleging that the petitioner was unauthorized constructing a pucca latrine on the khas land of the Government. It further appears that the respondent No.2 after initiation of the said proceeding issued the notice on the petitioner directing him to stop further proceedings with the construction of the latrine and asking him to show cause within 1-1-1994 why he should not be evicted from the aforesaid plot of land failing which legal action was ordered to be taken against the petitioner. 

 9. We have considered the materials available on record and the impugned Annexure 'D' and the aforesaid provision of the Ordinance. It appears to us that though no provision of law has been mentioned in the impugned Annexure 'D' it should be construed as a notice issued under section 5 of the Ordinance No. 24 of 1970. On a scrutiny of the relevant provision of Ordinance No. 24 of 1970 it appears to us that it is the Deputy Commissioner or an Additional Deputy Commissioner or a Joint Deputy Commissioner and such other persons as may be appointed by the Government to perform all or any of the functions of a Deputy Commissioner under the said Ordinance is lawfully competent to pass an order of eviction of an unauthorized occupier of Government khas land. In the present matter admittedly the Deputy Commissioner or an Additional Deputy Commissioner or a Joint Deputy Commissioner did not initiate the proceeding in question nor-passed the order as contained in impugned Annexure 'D'. It appears that there is nothing on record to satisfy us that the respondent No. 2 was appointed by the Government to perform the functions of a Deputy Commissioner as enjoined under Ordinance No. 24 of 1970. We have already noticed that the learned Assistant Attorney-General failed to produce anything before us to show that the respondent No. 2 were appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Deputy Commissioner for the purposes mentioned in Ordinance No. 24 of 1970. In view of the above we find that the respondent No. 2 was not competent to initiate the proceedings for eviction of the petitioner from the suit land and subsequently the issuance of the notice by the Annexure 'D' by the respondent No. 2 upon the petitioner is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. We therefore, find substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The initiation of the proceedings of the Miscellaneous (Eviction) Case No. 67 of 1993-94 and issuance of the show cause notice dated 15-12- 1993 as contained in Annexure 'D: is liable to be declared to have been taken and order passed by respondent No. 2 is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
